describesHead.landingTitle: docs(arch): define two-stage activation and the demand plan (#811)

rule: Each case states its input, the required and the forbidden outcome, the rules it exercises, existing evidence, and the node whose test makes it executable. TIF0 ships no test; the executable owner adds it. TC01-TC08 and TC11 are the fixtures the 2026-10-02 amendment moved to UAO0 subblock 3 (UAO0-AC-R2); TIF1 also runs TC08 for its compatibility projections (TIF1-AC3). Quality words are the TR24 vocabulary: Complete, Approximate { cause }, Unavailable { cause }. Every required outcome names the authority of each fact (TR21). A fact result names the InputBasisId it reports; a composed result names each child's InputBasisId and has no basis field (TR23). Existing evidence pins today's behaviour at the boundary the case replaces; an empty list means no current route exercises it.

cases.name: native-only
cases.input: types.ts declares `export interface Props { a: string; b?: number }`. A ResolveSymbol request names (SourceUnitId of types.ts, type namespace, `Props`) against the current view, Shallow mode, root-only closure. The request is then repeated with a different display policy.
cases.required: One fact, authority Native, quality Complete, provenance naming the decl-slot identity and the CD1 range of the declaration, and the InputBasisId of the captured view. Zero TypeScript backend calls. The repeat has the same QueryIdentity digest and the same fact; only the presentation differs.
cases.forbidden: A TypeScript query to confirm or enrich the fact; a fact without an authority; a result without a basis; a different QueryIdentity for a display-only change
cases.evidenceNote: The graph test pins the native answer; neither pins basis provenance or display-policy independence, which are new.

cases.name: TypeScript-authoritative
cases.input: A configured project with `const x = [1, 2].map(String)` in main.ts. A TypeAtPosition request selects the `x` identifier (SourceUnitId, CD1 offset, SourceRevision basis).
cases.required: One fact, authority TypeScript, quality Complete, basis = the certified PublishSnapshot input basis plus required_version, content_hash and map_hash; EngineIdentity and ProviderEpoch appear as provenance only. Zero native ProjectSemanticDispatch queries for that fact. With no configured project the fact is Unavailable { NoProject } and no native answer is produced.
cases.forbidden: A native recreation of the type; provider identity inside QueryIdentity; a BoundProject, binding or lease in the DTO; a native fallback when the project is missing
cases.evidenceNote: The binding is pinned; no TypeInfo operation reaches it yet (empty population).

cases.name: composed framework and TypeScript
cases.input: Comp.vue with `defineProps<{ item: Item }>()` where `Item` comes from a package whose declaration only the TypeScript program resolves (a `paths` mapping Verter does not own). A ComponentFacets request asks for props. That request matches only OP10's Composed claim (at least one requested facet needs a TypeScript fact), not the Native claim. A TypeAtPosition request selects `item` in the template. The binding of `item` is a framework fact, so the position is framework-bound and the request matches only OP11's Composed claim, not the TypeScriptAuthoritative claim.
cases.required: The props facet is a Framework fact (FrameworkProfileId, ReleaseId, macro provenance) whose Native child executes through ProjectSemanticDispatch. The member type of `item` is a TypeScript fact with its certified basis, and that child executes only through EngineBackend over CertifiedTypeEngineBinding. TIF1 is the composition owner and executes neither child. The composed result lists both facts with their own authorities and orders them canonically; its QueryIdentity is composed over the composition descriptor and the two child identities. It carries no basis field and no SemanticFlightKey. Each child result carries its own InputBasisId, and the ordered child bases are that sequence. TypeInfo defines no list, sum or wrapper to hold it. A follow-on NodeRef names a child fact, not the composition container.
cases.forbidden: Field-wise merge choosing one authority per field; the native engine answering the TypeScript-owned member type; one QueryIdentity for the composed and a child query; a composed InputBasisId, SemanticFlightKey, or TypeInfo-defined basis carrier; a NodeRef that names the composition container or coerces the child bases into an InputBasisId; matching both of OP10's claims or both of OP11's claims

cases.name: ambiguous
cases.input: Three requests. (a) A WorkspaceName selector `Button` where a.ts and b.ts both export `Button`. (b) A FileName selector `Foo` without namespace where one file declares `type Foo` and `const Foo`. (c) A FileName selector for a name declared by two owners of one SFC. Each is run with the files loaded in both orders.
cases.required: Each answers Ambiguous { candidates } with every candidate and its provenance, candidates in canonical order, identical under both load orders. Naming the file, the namespace or the owner selects exactly one candidate.
cases.forbidden: First-match, first-loaded or fastest candidate wins; silent fallback to the ordinary-file owner; the index answering a type fact; a warm cache entry claiming a single answer
cases.evidenceNote: Today the multi-owner case falls back silently (TIF-F03); no workspace selector exists.

cases.name: stale backend
cases.input: TC02's TypeAtPosition is answered and warmed. The provider then restarts (new serving session) and, separately, a new snapshot version is published without the client re-requesting.
cases.required: The warmed fact is not served for either change: it is Unavailable { StaleBackend } until a request under the live certified basis answers it. The stale answer never publishes and never warms, and StaleBackend publishes no refusal entry (TR31). A retry after resync answers what a fresh host answers.
cases.forbidden: Serving the old answer under a new serving session or snapshot version; warming an answer computed under a superseded basis

cases.name: changed map
cases.input: A TypeAtPosition request on a Vue template expression is answered through the IDE projection map. The expression is a projected template position in a configured project and its binding is not a framework fact, so the position is not framework-bound and the request matches only OP11's TypeScriptAuthoritative claim. The `<script>` block is then edited so the template bytes are unchanged but the projection MapRevision changes, and the same position is requested with the old basis.
cases.required: The old-basis request is refused (StaleSelector / changed map). A request with the new basis maps the position through the new MapRevision and answers fresh. No fact computed against the old map is served.
cases.forbidden: Approximate re-mapping of the old position; clamping to the nearest token; serving the old fact because the template bytes are equal
cases.evidenceNote: The certified Query already fails closed on content_hash/map_hash mismatch; no TypeInfo selector carries a map basis yet.

cases.name: missing input
cases.input: A ResolveSymbol request for an export of `vue` from a project whose node_modules is not captured (a prepared-input host that did not supply the package files), and a FileName selector whose path the registered source authority does not know.
cases.required: The first answers Unavailable { NeedInputs } naming the missing input, ReturnOnly. The second is a typed UnknownSource request error before execution. Supplying the input later answers fresh under a new basis.
cases.forbidden: Treating the missing package as an absent export; a guessed declaration; a scratch file minted for the unknown path; a warm negative entry
cases.evidenceNote: Today a missing export is a malformed payload or a graph fault; neither distinguishes a missing input from an absent declaration.

cases.name: composed-cache isolation
cases.input: TC03 warmed. Then, one at a time: the Vue release changes (new FrameworkProfileId); the TypeScriptSemanticProfileId changes (strict off); the `Item` declaration is edited; the same composition runs under a different evaluation context (another root's contextual typing).
cases.required: Each change misses the composed entry and recomputes only the children whose identity or basis changed; untouched children are reused. A composed entry never answers a child query and a child entry never answers the composed query. Incremental equals fresh after every change.
cases.forbidden: A composed hit across profiles, edits or contexts; a child served from the composed entry; recomputing unchanged children
cases.evidenceNote: Native edit invalidation is pinned; composed scope is new.

cases.name: identity excludes presentation, serialization and limits
cases.input: One ResolveSymbol request repeated with: a different display policy; a different schema version; provenance serialized and not serialized; a different work budget large enough to complete; a different requester encoding.
cases.required: All five share one QueryIdentity and one warm entry. A budget too small to complete returns a refusal whose identity names the budget profile, and a later larger budget recomputes and heals.
cases.forbidden: A distinct cache slot per display or schema variant; a budget-truncated value labelled Complete
cases.evidenceNote: Today provenance serialization is refused rather than served; GraphQueryIdentity mixes these fields (TIF-D03).

cases.name: deterministic ordering under schedule
cases.input: A ComponentFacets and a ResolveSymbol request over a union-heavy declaration, run with files loaded in reverse order, with a pre-warmed interner, and from two threads concurrently.
cases.required: Byte-identical results: facts, members and candidates in canonical order, union arms in VerterStableV1 order. A presentation request may reorder for display without changing equality.
cases.forbidden: Order that depends on load, interning, query or thread schedule; serialising allocation to make runs agree

cases.name: refusal reuse is not absence
cases.input: An isolated-root ResolveSymbol whose expansion exceeds its budget is refused. It is repeated under the same budget profile and root; then under a larger budget; then after an edit to a declaration it read.
cases.required: The same-profile repeat returns the stored refusal with zero producer work and stays a refusal. That stored refusal is the TR31 refusal-class entry; no fact, provenance or partial value is stored. The larger budget recomputes and answers. The edit invalidates the refusal. At no point does the refusal read as an absent symbol.
cases.forbidden: A refusal served as 'not found'; a refusal inherited by a different budget, root or demand epoch; a stale refusal after the edit
cases.evidenceNote: SKR-READS owns the refusal envelope; no TypeInfo route reuses a refusal yet.

cases.name: churn is not a miss
cases.input: A ResolveSymbol request issued while the host is under sustained mutation, so no current store view settles within the retry budget.
cases.required: Unavailable { UnsettledInput }, ReturnOnly, distinguishable on the wire from an unresolved name. UnsettledInput is not an eligible refusal and publishes no refusal entry (TR31). A request after the host settles answers fresh.
cases.forbidden: A null payload identical to 'could not be resolved'; a warm entry from the torn view
cases.evidenceNote: TIF-D05 is the route this replaces.

cases.name: unserved descriptor fails closed
cases.input: A request for each descriptor row the host does not serve yet, and for a selector kind its descriptor does not accept.
cases.required: A typed Unsupported refusal for an unserved row and a typed request error for an unaccepted selector, both before semantic execution.
cases.forbidden: Passing validation and returning nothing; a MalformedPayload for a well-formed but unserved operation
